question: Compute the Z-transform H(z) of h[n] = (1/2)**n * u[n].
_instructions: For each step set 'human_correct' to true/false. Set 'error_type' to one of: algebra, sign, missing_term, substitution, definition, none. Set '_filled' to true when done. Set 'final_answer_correct' to true/false after comparing 'generated_final' to 'expected_final'.

steps.description: Start with the definition of the Z-transform
Substitute h[n] = (1/2)^n * u[n] into the sum
Use the fact that u[n] is zero for n < 0 to change summation limits
steps.notes: u[n] truncates the lower limit to 0 and drops out.

steps.description: Combine terms into a single geometric sequence
Apply the formula for the sum of an infinite geometric series
steps.notes: Σ r^n = 1/(1−r) with r = (1/2)z^(-1); converges for |z|>1/2.

steps.description: Simplify the denominator by factoring out z in the denominator
steps.notes: Multiply numerator and denominator by z: 1/(1 − 1/(2z)) = z/(z − 1/2).
